experiment: ERA on AgentDescent -- SWE-bench Science, one tree per task
protocol: ERA's, not the benchmark's: the leaderboard gives an agent one attempt per task with no verifier feedback, while this scores a tree of agent sessions against the visible part of each private suite and keeps the best node. `benchmark_reward_*` is the release's own grader over the whole private suite; the search never reads it.

+def _nearest_most_frequent_sampling(
+    images,
+    mesh,
+    affine,
+    kind="auto",
+    radius=3.0,
+    n_points=None,
+    mask=None,
+    inner_mesh=None,
+    depth=None,
+):
+    """In each image, measure the intensity at each node of the mesh.
+
+    Each sample point is assigned the value of its nearest voxel, and the
+    value associated with a mesh vertex is the most frequent of the values
+    found at its sample points (ties are broken by the smallest value).
+
+    Unlike averaging schemes, this guarantees that every finite output
+    value is one of the values already present in the image, which is
+    required when the image is a discrete (e.g. label / atlas) volume
+    whose values must remain joinable to an external lookup table.
+
+    A 2-d array is returned, where each row corresponds to an image and each
+    column to a mesh vertex.
+    See documentation of vol_to_surf for details.
+
+    """
+    sample_locations = _sample_locations(
+        mesh,
+        affine,
+        kind=kind,
+        radius=radius,
+        n_points=n_points,
+        inner_mesh=inner_mesh,
+        depth=depth,
+    )
+    sample_locations = np.asarray(np.round(sample_locations), dtype=int)
+    n_vertices, n_points, _ = sample_locations.shape
+    interp_locations = np.vstack(sample_locations)
+    masked = _masked_indices(interp_locations, images[0].shape, mask=mask)
+    clipped = np.clip(
+        interp_locations, 0, np.asarray(images[0].shape) - 1
+    )
+    sample_mask = masked.reshape(n_vertices, n_points)
+    valid_vertices = ~sample_mask.all(axis=1)
+    all_textures = []
+    for img in images:
+        img = np.asarray(img)
+        samples = img[
+            clipped[:, 0], clipped[:, 1], clipped[:, 2]
+        ].astype(float)
+        samples = samples.reshape(n_vertices, n_points)
+        texture = np.full(n_vertices, np.nan)
+        best_counts = np.zeros(n_vertices)
+        valid_samples = samples[~sample_mask]
+        for value in np.unique(valid_samples):
+            counts = np.sum((samples == value) & ~sample_mask, axis=1)
+            better = valid_vertices & (counts > best_counts)
+            texture[better] = value
+            best_counts = np.maximum(best_counts, counts)
+        all_textures.append(texture)
+    return np.asarray(all_textures)
+
